title: Frequency
tagline: Father and son. Same radio. Same pizza.
about: A cop talks to his firefighter father across 30 years through an old ham radio.
cue: Serve dinner during the 1969 World Series broadcast.
faces: THE FIREHOUSE INVITES THE WHOLE BLOCK
GAME ONE ON THE RADIO AT NOON
Beef and kidney bean chilli in baked wonton cups, cheddar melted over.
Bicarb soda dip, coarse salt, baked glossy. Honey beer mustard.
Thin crust, crushed tomato, mozzarella and crumbled Italian sausage.
By the slice. Whole pie $1.69, boxed.
Meatballs in Sunday gravy on a long roll, provolone melted over.
Tart green apples, cinnamon and sugar, a double crust brushed with egg.
A frank on a buttered bun, chips and cold milk. Under seven.
Cold lager and fresh lemonade, mint sprig, lemon wheel. Grown-ups only.
Squeezed by the pitcher, over ice.
From the big percolator, all game long.
Our boys are in the Series and the block is family tonight. If the bell rings we roll, but the chilli stays hot. Over and out.
FOR THE MEN OF THE HOUSE
25¢, five for $1. See Frank or Satch.
Prices subject to change. Proceeds to the Widows and Orphans Fund.

    StartersChilli CupsBeef and kidney bean chilli in baked wonton cups, cheddar melted over.Ladled out the minute the anthem ends.How to make it12 wonton wrappers1 tsp oil, plus extra to grease200g beef mince1/2 onion, diced1 tsp chilli powder200g tinned chopped tomatoes120g tinned kidney beans, drained60g cheddar, gratedPress the wonton wrappers into a lightly oiled mini muffin tin. Bake at 180°C until crisp.Brown the mince in oil, add the onion and cook until soft.Stir in the chilli powder, tomatoes and beans. Simmer until thick.Spoon into the baked cups, top with cheddar and return to the oven to melt.Soft PretzelsBicarb soda dip, coarse salt, baked glossy. Honey beer mustard.Game One on the radio. Yahoo!How to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast1 tsp sugar1 tsp salt300ml warm water2 L water for boiling60g bicarb soda1 tbsp coarse salt100g wholegrain mustard2 tbsp lager1 tbsp honeyMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt and warm water and knead.Rise in a covered bowl until doubled.Shape into 8 pretzels.Boil each briefly in the water with the bicarb, then drain and sprinkle with coarse salt.Bake at 220°C until deep brown.Mix the mustard, lager and honey for the dip.MainsQueens Pizza PieThin crust, crushed tomato, mozzarella and crumbled Italian sausage.By the slice. Whole pie $1.69, boxed.How to make it380g bread flour2g dried yeast1 tsp salt245ml cool water200g Italian sausages200g crushed tomatoes200g low-moisture mozzarella, gratedMix the flour, yeast, salt and water and knead. Divide into two balls.Refrigerate covered to cold-ferment for a day or two.Bring to room temperature.Heat a pizza steel at the oven's maximum, about 250 to 275°C.Remove the sausage from its casings, crumble and pan-fry until cooked.Stretch the dough thin into two pizzas. Top with tomatoes, mozzarella and sausage.Bake each on the steel until crisp and cooked, then cut into wedges.SweetsJulia's Apple PieTart green apples, cinnamon and sugar, a double crust brushed with egg.Julia bakes it between shifts.How to make it400g sweet shortcrust pastry600g Granny Smith apples85g caster sugar1 tsp cinnamon15g plain flour1 egg, beatenLine a 20cm pie dish with half of the pastry.Peel, core and thinly slice the apples. Toss with sugar, cinnamon and flour.Fill the pastry, cover with the rest and crimp. Cut two steam vents, brush with egg and sprinkle with a little sugar.Bake at 190°C until golden and the apples are tender.Rest before cutting into four portions.DrinksFirehouse ShandyCold lager and fresh lemonade, mint sprig, lemon wheel.
